sessionTitle: Why your AI code doesn’t ship: Closing the gap to production

announcements.name: GitHub Copilot app
announcements.shortDescription: A newly launched surface positioned not as a session manager but as a tool to finish work, handling triage, CI, review feedback, merging, and deployment.
announcements.longDescription: The newly launched GitHub Copilot app is positioned not as just another session manager but as a tool built to help engineers finish work and deliver value to users. Rather than focusing on implementation or creating lots of parallel work, it handles the meta work around delivery: issue triage, getting through CI and keeping it green, responding to review feedback, merging, and getting changes deployed to customers. Evan Boyle, co-creator and engineering lead for the Cobalt CLI, Cobalt SDK, and the Copilot app, introduced it on stage.

announcements.name: Canvases
announcements.shortDescription: Agent-drivable, bidirectional UI surfaces (terminal, browser, triage boards, whiteboards, Kanban) that users or the agent can author dynamically and check into the repo's `.github` folder for team sharing.
announcements.longDescription: Canvases are agent-drivable UI surfaces within the Copilot app that the agent can fully drive on the right-hand side of the app, including a terminal canvas and a web browser. The agent can open the terminal, send commands, read output, open the browser, and perform automated testing in response to natural-language prompts. The demo showed asking the agent to open the terminal canvas, run a web server rendering 'Hello canvas', and then open the browser to render that page. Canvases support a rich bidirectional relationship and enable users to build their own customized views and workflows.

announcements.name: Canvas marketplace
announcements.shortDescription: A forthcoming marketplace for first- and third-party canvas extensions, including a Miro integration with agent-driven design boards.
announcements.longDescription: Alongside canvases, GitHub announced a forthcoming marketplace for canvas extensions, spanning both hyper-personalized miniature canvases and official first-party and third-party canvas extensions. The demo highlighted a Miro integration with an entire agent-driven design architecture, including feedback, sticky notes, and the rich features expected of Miro, but now agent-driven so the agent can make modifications and kick off implementation work. More official canvases from partners are described as coming soon, with more details about the Canvas marketplace to be shared.

announcements.name: Copilot `--cloud` on GitHub sandboxes
announcements.shortDescription: Stateful, isolated fast micro-VMs with tightly scoped credentials, letting users delegate tasks to run in the cloud overnight without keeping a laptop connected.
announcements.longDescription: Copilot `--cloud` lets users delegate tasks to run in the cloud so they can close their laptop and go home without keeping it connected to the internet. It is built on top of GitHub sandboxes, fast micro-VMs that spin up in a matter of seconds. The sandboxes are stateful and isolated, with tightly scoped credentials, so users can safely test out PRs separate from their laptop environment or kick off a task to run all night, ready to return to in the morning. The demo also showed switching into an autopilot 'Yolo' mode to run tasks in the cloud.

announcements.name: Chronicle
announcements.shortDescription: A private, per-user searchable record of every session, prompt, and line of code across all Copilot surfaces, queryable by the agent via a direct SQL API plus full-text search; supports features like `Chronicle stand up`.
announcements.longDescription: Chronicle is a per-user, private record of all of your sessions, scoped to your user and only accessible to you, providing continuity across surfaces, machines, and different GitHub Copilot products. It remembers everything you have ever done — every session, every line of code, every prompt — and can crawl through that history to find relevant context, such as how a prior Rust bug was fixed, and load it into the current session. The agent queries Chronicle using a combination of full-text search and structured SQL queries over a data lake of sessions, exposed via a direct SQL API. It also powers features like `Chronicle stand up`, which reviews work done in the last 24 hours.

announcements.name: Agent Merge
announcements.shortDescription: An agentic automation that monitors a PR, resolves merge conflicts, keeps CI green, and addresses review feedback until the PR is ready, while pushing back on unreasonable requests.
announcements.longDescription: Agent Merge is an agentic automation surfaced as a button on a pull request that focuses on getting work over the line. Once clicked, it periodically checks in on the PR to see whether there are merge conflicts, whether CI is green, and whether there is feedback from an agent or a coworker that needs to be resolved, making all of those changes until the PR is green and ready to go. The demo referenced the very first Agent Merge PR, created by Jeremy on March 19th, which added a CLI health check and went through rounds of CCR (Copilot code review) feedback.

announcements.name: Automations
announcements.shortDescription: Scheduled or event-triggered agent jobs (e.g., a 6 AM local "morning brief," or a cloud automation that reproduces bug reports and writes failing test cases on issue creation).
announcements.longDescription: Automations are scheduled or event-triggered agent jobs used to guard a developer's focus amid a fire hose of feedback sources across public, private, and Slack Connect channels. The demo showed a 'morning brief' automation that runs at 6:00 AM every day locally on the presenter's machine, summarizing in-flight PRs that need to get over the line, critical unreviewed PRs blocking other engineers, and new critical issues. Mario noted that Agent Merge is itself a type of agentic automation running locally, and that automations could be extended across the entire software development lifecycle.

announcements.name: Rubber Duck
announcements.shortDescription: A multi-mode agent (advisor and critic) available in the Copilot CLI and Copilot app for getting a second opinion on work.
announcements.longDescription: Rubber Duck [inferred] (heard as 'Rover Duck') is an agent for getting a second opinion on your work, made possible because GitHub is multi-model, multi-agent, and multi-surface. It operates in two modes: as an advisor and as a critic, bringing the kind of collaboration developers normally do with other humans into human-and-agent collaboration. It is available in the Copilot CLI (heard as 'Caballo CLI' [inferred Cobalt]) and now also in the GitHub app, where the presenter says he uses it constantly, mainly in critique mode and sometimes in assistance mode to save tokens.

announcements.name: Multi-model code and security review
announcements.shortDescription: Slash commands (`/review`, `/security review`) orchestrate parallel sub-sessions using multiple models (Gemini, GPT, Claude Sonnet 4.6), built with GitHub Advanced Security.
announcements.longDescription: The Copilot app acts as an orchestrator that can compose review workflows together using slash commands: `/review` for code review and `/security review` for security. These can run as parallel sub-sessions using multiple models — Gemini, GPT, and Claude Sonnet 4.6 — which, because they have different training distributions and don't always agree, yield the best possible results. In the demo, the presenter asked the agent to use the create session tool to run one session doing a multi-model code review with Gemini, GPT-5 [inferred, heard as 'GPT 55'], and Sonnet 4.6, and a second session running a multi-model security review, then to rubber duck the combined output critically and optionally post comments to the pull request.
